messages:
tara: Quick question about /v1/embeddings — want to confirm contract for empty strings vs nulls and whether batch responses always preserve input order. Updating the Python SDK this morning.
jon: short answer: order should be preserved, but double-checking null vs empty behavior.
priya: current impl: explicit null in the input => we return null for that index. empty string ("") is a valid input and we run it through the encoder, so you get a real vector (not zeros). there was a batching edge-case that dropped placeholders though.
jon: yeah that batching bug (missing placeholder write) got introduced when we switched async scatter-gather. fix is in PR but not yet deployed.
alex: PR #4321 adds placeholder handling and unit test. will canary tonight. @tara please validate once up.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for service=embeddings image=redwood/embeddings:v2.4 at 2026-03-15T02:00:00Z
tara: thanks. another Q: truncation — do we truncate per-item or across the whole batch? and is it token-based (preferred) or char-based in the contract?
jon: truncation is per-item. pipeline: tokenize(item) -> if tokens > model_max_tokens then drop tail tokens (right-truncate) -> embed. we do not concat items; no cross-item trimming.
priya: model_max_tokens currently 2048 for fast-embed-1536. clients should expect token-level truncation. we still accept very long raw strings but they get token-trimmed.
tara: great — and batch size limits?
jon: API returns 400 if items > 256 in a single request. that's enforced at the gateway. consider chunking.
priya: small nuance: we allow a mix of strings and objects (legacy) in the payload; make sure SDK normalizes to [string|null].
tara: can you paste the expected response shape so I mirror it exactly in the SDK?
jon: sure — example:

```
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {"object": "embedding", "index": 0, "embedding": [0.00123, -0.0023, ...]},
    {"object": "embedding", "index": 1, "embedding": null}
  ],
  "model": "redwood/fast-embed-1536",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": "123"}
}
```

jon: notes: - index field maps to original input order. - embedding is either an array of floats (length = 1536 for that model) or null. - we keep object:"list" for compatibility.
priya: confirm: embedding vectors are dense floats (float32) serialized as JSON numbers. length fixed per model when non-null.
tara: perfect. I'll map null -> None in Python and keep empty-string -> vector. also will add retry for 429 and chunking for >256.
alex: updated docs in /docs/embeddings.md with the tokens/batch table and an explicit example. ping me if anything else.
tara: awesome, thanks — will open a tiny follow-up PR for SDK once canary is green. :thumbsup:\n
